speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have experienced an episode of loss of consciousness; please sit down and tell me exactly what happened right before and after you fainted. Were you alone, and did anyone witness the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tachycardia-Cataplexy (Tic Cataplexy). The patient's history of loss of consciousness immediately after urination is a classic presentation of this rare disorder, often mistaken for syncope or epilepsy. I need to confirm the specific trigger and rule out other causes like cardiac arrhythmia or epilepsy.

REQUEST TEST: ECG, EEG, Cardiac_Monitoring, MRI_Brain.
